basis: snapshot narrativeCache.data — compact read: recommendation, coreAnalysis, pool openings, bridge, scenarios.

justifications.depth: AI Accelerators (~660 words) and Server CPUs (~550) carry the argument with real economics; Client and Embedded drop to ~200 words each and state their required EBITDA without deriving it.
justifications.coverage: Five divisions, each with an EV share and a required-EBITDA test, and the Embedded allocation is correctly explained as asset- and goodwill-backed rather than earnings-backed.
justifications.logic: The central requirement is quantified and checkable — roughly 2.5m Instinct units at a USD 12,500 blended ASP with a 40% operating margin — and the FCF bridge (negative USD 10.5bn in 2026 on a USD 9.4bn working-capital build) is treated as the real constraint rather than a footnote.
justifications.evidence: EPYC at 46.2% revenue and 33.2% unit share, Nvidia at ~85% share with USD 25–40k ASPs, the Xilinx goodwill and intangible balances — specific and consistent with the tables. TAM figures are management guidance, correctly attributed as such.
justifications.valuation: Two sound legs (25.0x 2028e EBITDA, 35.0x P/E) are blended with an ROE/P-BV scatter leg implying USD 122.8 — a quarter of the other two — at 10% weight. Averaging a method that disagrees by 4x does not make the target more robust. The Base scenario again lands within 2% of spot.
justifications.readability: Well structured; the Gaming division renders as a grouped summary with an empty deep dive.

summary: Solid work on a company where the option is priced in silicon rather than in narrative: the AI-accelerator requirement is stated as units, ASP and margin, and the cash-flow constraint is honest. The bridge is let down by a scatter leg that disagrees with the other methods by 4x and a Base scenario calibrated to spot.
issues: ROE/P-BV leg implies USD 122.8 against USD 500–552 from the other legs
Gaming pool renders with an empty deep dive
